info.text:
Some movers load your stuff, then hold it for ransom.

It's called a hostage load: a cheap quote, then a much bigger bill once your things are on the truck.
Hostage-load complaints to DOT went from 364 in 2017 to 899 in 2020 (FMCSA data via AARP). In April 2024, a three-week FMCSA sweep still addressed 128 hostage complaints.
Ohio federal prosecutors said one ring running more than a dozen rogue moving companies (2013-2018) cost victims over $2.4 million.
FMCSA red flags: cash or a large deposit, no in-home or virtual survey, no "Your Rights and Responsibilities When You Move" booklet. Check the USDOT number on FMCSA's site and report problems to FMCSA's National Consumer Complaint Database. Federal law sets a civil penalty of at least $10,000 per violation for holding goods hostage.

Sources: FMCSA Protect Your Move and Operation Protect Your Move reports (2023, 2024); AARP (Aug 2021); U.S. Attorney, S.D. Ohio; 49 U.S.C. 14915.
News and education, not financial advice.
